Sharhorod Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the oldest of Sharhorod's three documented Jewish cemeteries, established according to IAJGS sometime between 1590 and 1648, and located today in the very center of town — a notable contrast to most cemeteries in this collection, which tend to have been pushed to town outskirts. Sharhorod's Jewish community, once the largest in Podolia at 2,219 people in 1765, was converted into a well-organized ghetto during Romanian administration, complete with its own bakeries, pharmacy, hospital, and orphanage; unusually, the majority of the roughly 7,000 Jews held there by December 1941 survived the war, and a Jewish community of about 700 people still existed in Sharhorod in the 1990s.
